transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Welcome, everyone, to Devils Tower National Monument. Not only can you view the famous Devils Tower rock formation, but there are lots of great routes for hiking and rock-climbing here in the park. If you are interested, you can ask about those activities at our climbing office.
transcript.highlight_text: ask about those activities at our climbing office

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: You’ll find it conveniently located between our visitor centre and gift shop. Now, Devils Tower is situated in the picturesque Black Hills here in Wyoming. The formation itself is very imposing, standing at 867 feet, or 265 metres, from the base to the summit.

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: To local Native Americans, this is a significant site. Because of that and its striking beauty, Devils Tower was made an official national monument over a century ago.
transcript.highlight_text: Devils Tower was made an official national monument

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Since then, it has become a popular destination amongst rock climbers. So how did the rock formation get its unusual name? You might think it’s because it can be dangerous to hike up or climb. Actually, explorer Colonel Richard Irving led an expedition to the area in 1875.

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: His interpreter is said to have made an error translating the native language, and said the unusual formation was named ‘Bad God’s Tower.’ Irving took that to mean the Devil’s Tower ... but many native people say that the formation was probably originally called ‘Bear Tower’ or ‘Bear’s Lodge.’
transcript.highlight_text: His interpreter is said to have made an error translating the native language

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Anyway, what are we all going to see and do at the park today? First, we are going to take a short hike up to a ridge that will offer you panoramic views of the tower and the park. The route we will be taking is called the Joyner Ridge Trail, and it is a marked loop that’s a mile and a half long.

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Just a few safety reminders before we head out on the trail. First, please watch your step during our hike as the trail we are taking is unpaved. Also, please be reminded that food is only permitted in specified areas that are marked with signs, and it is vital that you do not feed animals you may encounter in the park.
transcript.highlight_text: it is vital that you do not feed animals you may encounter in the park

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: After our hike, I’ll take you to the visitor centre where you can check out our displays and browse through souvenirs in our gift shop. OK. So, could you all please come this way?
